C11 is a broader resignation-letter precedent but is temporally remote and lacks the distinctive end-of-term formulation.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I have your letter of resignation, effective at the end of my term, January 20, 1953, and I accept it","parent_excerpt":"I have your letter and I accept your resignation as Secretary of Defense, effective at the end of the President's term of office, January 20, 1953","explanation":"Distinctive near-verbatim opening formula combining receipt, acceptance, end-of-term effectiveness, and the exact date."},{"child_excerpt":"I accept it with warm thanks for a job well done.","parent_excerpt":"As we both prepare to leave office, I thank you for your devotion and your wisdom and your skill.","explanation":"Both couple the end-of-administration resignation with direct personal thanks for distinguished service."},{"child_excerpt":"Certainly no man is more responsible than you for pulling together the people of the free world, and strengthening their will and their determination to be strong and free.","parent_excerpt":"The splendid achievements of the Department of Defense in these last years must be attributed in large part to your vision and deep understanding of international as well as domestic affairs.","explanation":"Parallel central praise credits the departing secretary personally for major international and national-security achievements."}]}
